EWI to lead $13.2M America Makes metal AM quality-assurance project

America Makes · 9/10

Metal Additive Manufacturing magazine reports that EWI will lead a $13.2M America Makes project on quality assurance for metal additive manufacturing. Quality assurance, meaning confirming that printed parts are sound, is a major hurdle for industrial metal 3D printing. Only the headline is available, so the project's scope and sensors are unconfirmed.

Small-data neural ensemble predicts Heisenberg exchange J within 1% error

arXiv · magnetism + ML · 8/10

The abstract reports an ensemble of dense neural networks that predicts Heisenberg exchange J, the coupling between neighboring magnetic spins, from crystal structure and composition. It was trained on only a few hexagonal manganites and generalized to other compounds in that family at random geometries. Learning exchange from small datasets could speed up screening of magnetic materials, but transfer beyond one chemical family still needs to be shown.

Quantum benchmarks test (S+1)/S rescaling of classical Monte Carlo T_C

arXiv · magnetism + ML · 7/10

The abstract reports that an (S+1)/S rescaling cut the mean gap between classical and quantum estimates of the critical temperature from 81.7 K to 8.2 K across 17 compounds. The compounds were described by Heisenberg models derived from inelastic neutron scattering. If it holds more broadly, a simple correction could make cheap classical simulations of magnets far more useful.

Baxter-Wu benchmark shows free-exponent fits bias critical amplitudes

arXiv · statistical mechanics · 8/10

Using exact Baxter-Wu results as a benchmark, the authors find that corrections to scaling make a local effective exponent drift. A free-exponent fit on a plateau absorbs that drift and biases the fitted amplitudes, while a fixed-exponent fit that includes the correction series matches the exact values. It is a useful warning for anyone extracting critical behavior from simulation data.

ML · Magnetic Materials

CoTiO3 anisotropy traced to bond-dependent Ising-like orbital exchange

J. Magnetism & Magnetic Materials · 7/10

The title points to CoTiO3 magnetic anisotropy arising from bond-dependent Ising-like orbital interactions coupled to the lattice. No abstract is available, so the details of how the anisotropy was established are unconfirmed. Anisotropy, or a preferred direction for magnetization, is central to permanent magnets and data storage.

UniHam: 100k+ spin-orbit-complete DFT Hamiltonians for ML benchmarking

arXiv · ML materials discovery · 6/10

The abstract reports UniHam, a dataset of over 100,000 DFT Hamiltonians with full spin-orbit coupling across 72 elements, along with out-of-distribution test sets. Spin-orbit coupling is a main source of magnetocrystalline anisotropy, so data like this could eventually support machine-learning models for that property. It is a benchmark resource rather than a new material or result.

Paired dopants in 2D MoSe2 give large MAE and ~440 K Tc

arXiv · magnetism + ML · 6/10

DFT+U calculations report in-plane magnetic anisotropy energy (MAE) of up to -3.5 meV, and a Monte Carlo Curie temperature of about 440 K, for a 2Fe dopant pair in monolayer MoSe2. It is a worked example of combining anisotropy, exchange and Monte Carlo estimates in one system. The work concerns semiconductor doping, and the Tc is a model prediction rather than an experimental measurement.

Graph network maps PBE energies to r2SCAN-level accuracy

npj Computational Materials · 5/10

The abstract reports a graph neural network trained on 380,190 paired PBE and r2SCAN calculations, reaching a mean absolute error of 14.3 meV/atom. PBE is a widely used DFT functional, so a correction like this could make large materials databases more accurate. Formation energies are not magnetic labels, so whether the approach works for magnetic systems is an open question.

Additive Manufacturing

AgentAM: LLM agent queries CFD-trained spatter and melt-pool surrogates

arXiv · AM monitoring & physics · 6/10

The abstract reports polynomial surrogates trained on 279 single-track simulations, with spatter R² of 0.83 and a defect-regime match of 93.4% under cross-validation. The surrogates are accessed through an LLM agent. Because the work is simulation-only, it has no in-situ sensor data or X-ray CT ground truth, and its defect regimes are derived from geometry rather than measured defects.

Dual-loop policy-optimization controller stabilizes LPBF surface temperature

Additive Manufacturing (journal) · 5/10

The abstract reports a dual-loop policy-optimization controller for laser powder bed fusion that stabilizes surface temperature. Physical LPBF validation showed a 3.4% reduction in mean tracking error compared with a Bayesian-optimization baseline, and the controller was tuned offline from one calibration layer. It is a control result rather than a sensing one, but it shows how thermal feedback can steer printing. Whether a 3.4% gain exceeds run-to-run variation is not stated.

Velo3D signs five-year research agreement with Sandia

News · AM policy & funding · 6/10

Only the headline is available: Velo3D, a metal laser powder bed fusion vendor, has signed a five-year research agreement with Sandia National Laboratories. Partnerships like this can generate process and qualification data for metal printing. Details of the work and whether any public data will result are unconfirmed.

Velo3D secures $11.5M defense contract

News · AM policy & funding · 6/10

Only the headline is available: Velo3D has secured an $11.5M defense contract. Defense contracts are one channel through which U.S. additive manufacturing is funded. Contract terms, including any qualification or in-process monitoring requirements, are unconfirmed.

Theoretical Physics

Cycle-space Wang-Landau computes Ising partition functions at all temperatures

arXiv · spin models & criticality · 7/10

The abstract reports rewriting the Ising partition function as a sum over even subgraphs and sampling that space with a 1/t Wang-Landau random walk. A single estimate yields thermodynamics at any temperature. The method was validated against exact results for the triangular-lattice Ising model and tested on 3D and 4D Ising and Baxter-Wu models, but its handling of anisotropic, non-uniform couplings from real crystal structures is not covered here.

Zigzag ladder with anisotropic Γ term has gapped phases except isotropic case

arXiv · spin models & criticality · 7/10

The abstract reports exact diagonalization and DMRG results for a zigzag spin ladder with an anisotropic Γ term, a model tied to the material YbCuS2. The Néel, dimer, ferromagnetic and double-Néel phases are all gapped, and the gapless Tomonaga-Luttinger phase appears only in the isotropic case without the Γ term. It is a clear example of how anisotropic exchange can reshape a quantum magnet's phase diagram.

Can gravity's quantum nature show up without entanglement?

arXiv · quantum physics · 6/10

Physicists often test whether gravity is quantum by asking if two masses can become entangled through gravity, but environmental noise usually destroys that entanglement. The abstract reports a proof that, even when the state stays separable (unentangled), gravitational phase evolution can still be told apart from classical-noise models. The result holds under stated assumptions about the classical mediator, and it widens the experimental window for testing quantum gravity.

Strong Mpemba effect demonstrated in a single optical qubit

Phys.org · Quantum physics · 6/10

The Mpemba effect is when a system starting farther from equilibrium relaxes faster than one starting closer to it. The strong version means the farther system relaxes exponentially faster. This experiment reports the strong effect in a single optical qubit, a clean demonstration of a nonequilibrium result. Only a teaser is available, so details are unconfirmed.

HyProMag USA advances Texas rare-earth magnet plant with equipment delivery

Several outlets, including Sharecast and ACCESS Newswire, report the first major equipment delivery for HyProMag USA's rare-earth magnet plant in North Texas. GKN Aerospace gets first Nadcap accreditation for wire-DED process

News · AM policy & funding · 5/10

Machinery.co.uk reports that GKN Aerospace has received Nadcap accreditation for its wire-based directed energy deposition method, L-DED-w. Nadcap is an aerospace industry accreditation program for special processes, so this is a qualification milestone. It is not laser powder bed fusion, and the monitoring evidence the accreditation required is not described.
